To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 8p23p23 deletion and a 12p13p13 duplication, in a patient with neurocognitive and behavioral disturbances and epilepsy, may be associated with a distinct phenotype.

1) the 8p monsomy phenotype is characterized by severe ID, facial dysmorphism (including hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and downslanting palpebral fissures), and CNS anomalies (such as corpus callosum agenesis, and ventricular dilatation); 2) 12p trismoy is associated with mild ID, behavioral disturbances (including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and autistic spectrum disorders (ASD)),
the patient had a de novo 6.86-Mb 8p23p23 deletion, a 8.49-Mb 12p13p13 duplication, and an array CGH analysis was performed.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the genetic basis for ID, and other developmental abnormalities, and with the delineation of the genotype/phenotype correlation for partial monosomies of the short arm, and partial trisomies of the proximal region of the short arm in chromosome 12, which are rare, but clinically significant, genetic disorders.
the characterization of a new case of partial 8p monsomy and 12p trsomy, and with genotype/phenotype correlations.
the characterization of an unusual genomic aberration, with a description of the patient’s phenotype and long-term follow-up.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phenotype of the patient is the result of the interaction between the two chromosomal aberrations.
8p monsomy is associated with ID, facial dysmorphism and epilepsy, while 12p tricomy is associated with behavioral disturbances, and EEG abnormalities.
the 12p duplication, and the 8p deletion, are both necessary to cause this syndrome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the presence of a de novo 12p duplication, a 8p deletion is more likely to cause ID than a 12p duplication.
the 8p23 deletion and 12p13 duplication, are likely to be responsible for the clinical features observed in the patient.
the clinical picture is more severe than expected, and that the clinical features in our case are more in line with 8p monosomes than with 12p trismies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the clinical phenotype associated to partial 8p monsomy and partial 12p triplosomy is complex and heterogeneous, with a wide spectrum of clinical features and a large overlap with those associated to 8p23 deletion and 12p duplication syndromes, as well as with other chromosomal syndromes.
the clinical features of our case are consistent with the phenotype of partial 8p monsomy and 12p trismoy.
, even though 8p23 and 12p13 are small genomic regions, they contain a large number of genes, and the phenotypic consequences of their imbalance can be significant
